raw_response:
I am an old farmer, and I do not like changing too much unless I see a clear reason. This year I will still keep most of my land in wheat-maize, because that is what feeds the family and brings steady money. I will leave a smaller piece for millet. Millet does not need as much water or fertilizer, so it helps me keep some safety if the weather turns bad or if I do not want to spend too much cash at one time. Some people in my family work outside, so I cannot depend on everyone being home every day. Because of that, I will do the work in a simple way, mostly the same as before: wheat gets base fertilizer and one topdress, maize goes in quickly right after wheat harvest, and millet stays on the lighter land where it can manage with fewer inputs. I have a well, so if it stays dry I will irrigate, but I will not pump more than needed because electricity and water both cost money.
